title: Shaar HaYichud ch 33 (classes 033.1 and 033.2): hisbonenus of the upper unity

lectures.id: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3
Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

overview: Chapter 33 applies the *hisbonenus* of the first nine chapters to the upper unity (*yichuda ila'a*), which the class treats as one descent. It begins with G-d's essential desire for kindness, the *hiyuli* will within the *Or Ein Sof*. That desire rises to do good in a particular way and passes through the vessels, but everything stays *Ein Sof*. It contracts through the circles (*igulim*) and the line (*Kav*), through *Adam Kadmon* and the attributes of *Abba* and *Ima*, to the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, and each stage looks separate from its source. The whole descent happens at once, because G-d, His life and His organs are one. *Zeir Anpin* is the small face: it has the same makeup as *Arich Anpin*, expressed in small things, as a child has the same makeup as an elder. The examples are a map that holds the whole earth at a small scale, a child's emotions, and a sprout that shows its quality. The chapter closes with practice: contemplating this while davening lets a person say the simple words with deeper faith and trust, and accept his place in the mission.

terms.gloss: contemplation: seeing the many details as one idea, a single klal that includes them

raw, formless potential; G-d's essential desire for kindness, before any structure

sections.title: The first major stop: many details, one idea
sections.summary: Chapter 33 is the first class that puts the whole upper unity together and applies the *hisbonenus* taught in the first nine chapters. It opens by recalling that the teaching so far has been a chain of levels, and then reads the chapter's opening lines, which say that *hisbonenus* is one idea made of many details, all connected to one *klal*.

blocks.text: This is the first major stop. The first nine chapters of *Shaar HaYichud* explained *hisbonenus* (contemplation) with only small examples. Chapters 10 to 32 built the upper unity (*yichuda ila'a*), from the light before the *tzimtzum* (contraction) down through the lights and vessels of *Zeir Anpin* (the small face). Chapter 33 applies *hisbonenus* to all of it at once: to see each level and how they link, like the links of a chain, until one can run from the top to the bottom as if it were one thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Learning to read
blocks.text: It is like learning to read. At first you sound out each letter, but later you read without noticing the letters, and the meaning goes through all those levels at once.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The phone call
blocks.text: When you speak on the phone, you do not think about the satellites, the wiring of the brain and the ear, or how the sound is rebuilt. It happens as one step, and you say, "I'm talking to them." We want to understand these ideas well enough to condense them, so that we can say simply that G-d does whatever He wants, and see that in a deeper way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Now the first line can be understood. *Hisbonenus* is one idea made of many details, and every detail connects to one *klal*, one general principle that includes them all.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The verse says that whatever G-d desires, He does in heaven and earth. This has two sides. Whatever G-d wants, He can do. And everything that is created is according to His desire: no other force or input exists, and His wisdom and preferences are expressed in every detail.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: G-d's desire goes back to its original source, before the *tzimtzum*, in the *chafetz chesed*, on the level of *Yachid*.

The Mitteler Rebbe raised near the start of the book, in chapter 3 he thinks, how to use all this learning in davening. The verse from Psalms, 'whatever G-d desires He does, in the heavens, the earth, the seas and all the depths,' shows how.

sections.title: G-d's essential desire, and how it descends within Ein Sof
sections.summary: Before any world exists, G-d's essential desire for kindness is the *hiyuli* will within the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*. The desire rises to do good in a particular way and descends through the vessels of the heart, but everything is still *Ein Sof*, estimated within G-d himself. The class then digresses on the teaching that one favor can be the whole purpose of a soul.

phrases.en: this is G-d's essential desire for kindness, this *hiyuli* essential desire within the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, that's completely simple.

phrases.en: the analogy we gave for that is like a person's desire for kindness that's imprinted within the essence of their soul

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב באות יו''ד)

blocks.text: This is G-d's essential desire for kindness: the *hiyuli* desire within the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, which is completely simple.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Kindness in the soul
blocks.text: A person's kindness is imprinted in the essence of his soul, connected to nothing outside him.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: One basis of belief in G-d's oneness is to recognize that He is totally beyond time, space and all the considerations of the world. So His desire cannot be described in terms of the world's needs.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Needs and the inner self
blocks.text: A person has needs: food, shelter, things he wants. Before those, one can look inward and find a part of himself outside the world, which is simply who he is.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Two people in one situation
blocks.text: Later that inner part meets the world, and our nature plugs into it. Two people in the same circumstances can react differently, because of what is inside them. So G-d's essential desire transcends the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: G-d has an essential ability to create something from nothing. For reasons beyond anything in the world, He chose to express that by making the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Once we have this understanding, we do not picture G-d as a magical being. G-d sets the rules of creation, time and space, and even the *sefiros*, and He transcends all of them. He makes the rules and decides how everything will be.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32. This is its explanation of the essential will of line 3, placed here.

blocks.text: What is essentially desired has intrinsic value: the Jewish people, Torah and mitzvos. All the way down, in Zeir Anpin, we get what we do, measure for measure.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32. This is its explanation of the essential will of line 3, placed here.

blocks.text: On one level we get what we do; on a higher level G-d gives existence and meaning beyond that. Keser is the thirteen attributes of mercy, an intrinsic mercy and value that we have.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: When the desire to do good in a particular way rose out of the general light of the *hiyuli*, it descended through His essence, still within the *Ein Sof*, until it reached *netzach* and *hod*, the external vessels of the heart. The external attributes of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* are beyond any limiting of lights in vessels, yet everything is still *Ein Sof* itself. G-d estimated all of this within Himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The descent reaches the vessels of *netzach* and *hod* in the *kli halev*, which is what chapter 32 finished: the external vessels of *Zeir Anpin*. From there comes *hashgacha prati*: how G-d designs the world, His preferences of what is good and bad, pure and impure, and what He wants to influence in the physical world, from people to angels to trees. All of these preferences were first estimated within Himself, in the *Ein Sof*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: All of this is self-expression. G-d decides how He wants to reveal Himself, a certain light and flavor of Himself, and those decisions later become what happens in the *seder hishtalshelus*. At this point it is only G-d deciding how He wants to reveal Himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Inner taste becomes every detail
blocks.text: G-d set within Himself how this would play out, though no limits of lights in vessels yet existed. Compare the metaphor of chapters 15 to 17: a person's inner taste and preferences become expressed outwardly, the difference between *ratzon hamuchlat* and *ratzon kadum*. The inner taste becomes the source of every detail.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Everything is still totally infinite within Himself. In *avoda* this shows in the teaching of *Hayom Yom*: a *neshama* comes down for seventy or eighty years just to do one favor for another Jew. In the light of all creation, a whole life is worth that one action, which expresses the essence in one small thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *Rebbe* says that every person is a microcosm that expresses the purpose of all creation. So is every year and every day: waking is like being born, the day is one's work, and saying the *Shema* at night is returning the soul.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Look at it from the deeper perspective of G-d's infinite essence, and find a way to express that G-dly taste today. Today itself must be made G-dly, not only a matter of yesterday or tomorrow. As a person's taste shows in every detail of what he does, G-dliness is found in every detail.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Every letter of the Torah is G-d's name and holy, even where it looks like an external historical detail. Seen from this perspective, everything expresses G-d's essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Which favor?
blocks.outOfPlace: A digression after the explanation of lines 4 to 6, not a reading of them: the class leaves the text here for the teaching on a soul's favor.
blocks.text: If one favor is the whole reason the soul came down, and the soul did many favors in seventy or eighty years, which one was it? We don't know which one it is, so it could be any one. The real idea is to treat every opportunity to do a favor as the whole reason I am here. Because G-d put me in this situation today, that justifies everything, if I plug into it and do something of meaning.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Plugging in at every moment
blocks.outOfPlace: Continues the digression on a soul's favor, which the class does not tie back to these lines.
blocks.text: A favor done as a means to an end, to rack up brownie points for the next world or to bring *Moshiach*, means that right now I am not really plugged in. I am not putting my whole essence into the moment. The point of the teaching is to plug in at every moment, not to wait for one moment that does it, with my whole *yechida* and *bechol me'odecha*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Eliyahu in disguise
blocks.outOfPlace: A story in the digression on a soul's favor, placed where the class tells it.
blocks.text: From the time of the *Baal Shem Tov*, or before, the *tzaddikim* told stories of *Eliyahu HaNavi* appearing as a simple person. The idea is to treat a simple person one does not know as if he were *Eliyahu* in disguise. In truth that person is a literal piece of G-d, greater than my concept of *Eliyahu*, and deserves the same care and respect.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Continues the digression on the *tzaddikim*'s stories, which the class does not tie back to these lines.
blocks.text: The stories are not literally true, and in a way they are more true than that. From a deeper, more mature view they are true in a different way, more real and more constant.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

sections.title: The igulim, the yosher, and the descent to the vessels of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: G-d's will comes down from its essence through circles (*igulim*), a line (*Kav*), the associations of *Adam Kadmon*, and the attributes of *Abba* and *Ima*, to the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*. Each stage is a self-expression that looks separate from its source.

phrases.en: and then

blocks.text: Look at everything from this perspective: everything is G-d expressing Himself. Every leaf and every rock is holy. This is the *Baal Shem Tov*'s idea of *hashgacha prati*: every little detail of creation is essential, because it expresses a deeper G-dly essence, higher than any purpose that comes from the world, and infinite.

blocks.text: G-d brought that essential desire down through a *tzimtzum*, making the world seem separate from Himself. The *Kav*, a finite line of light, creates a hierarchy: a challenge, a tutorial with higher and lower levels, which we work our way up.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The ultimate goal is to bring *Moshiach*, which is the *ratzon kadum*, the first general desire for a *dira b'tachtonim*: the mission to reveal G-d's essence in the lowest realm, which seems very separate and opposite to Him. Before that, the essence passes through the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*, as the chapters on the *igulim* explained.

blocks.text: The *Kav* creates the relationship of *mashpia* and *mekabel*, above and below. In G-d's essence there is no up and down; now He is the giver and we are the receivers. In the *igulim* He plugs in His essential desire as a desire for something outside Himself.

blocks.title: A house to feel at home in
blocks.text: A person has an inner taste, the *ratzon hamuchlat*, and then a desire for a house outside himself. What he really wants is to feel at home, to be himself and express his real self. In this world we are stuck outside and must find what can plug in that inner desire. So people look at the houses, the little boxes with numbers and name tags, and make a house their desire. From an airplane the houses look small, which gives perspective.

blocks.text: Next is *yosher*, the difference between the *igulim* and the *ratzon hamuchlat* before the *tzimtzum*. The latter is like a person's taste, not yet plugged into the outside world.

blocks.title: Personality
blocks.text: A person is born with a personality, which he shapes a little through his choices and experiences. G-d decided to create a persona for Himself: out of infinite possibilities, He chose to express one aspect of Himself, one flavor, through this world. That is the limited light He chooses to express.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The author and his characters
blocks.text: The self-expression before the *tzimtzum* is the estimation within Himself, and the *ratzon kadum* is that desire appearing as something outside Him. Like an author who writes a story, the characters and the whole world are inside him. Each takes a bit of his personality and experiences, and together they explore a theme. Seen from before the *tzimtzum*, we are all sparks, aspects of G-d.

blocks.title: Dreams and imagination
blocks.text: The *tzimtzum* lets G-d make things feel separate from Himself. We have a limited version: in a dream we create characters and experience them as outside us, though it all happens inside us. With G-d's thought, it becomes reality.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: In the metaphor there is a teacher and a student, so the teacher must express things in a limited way. With G-d, the limiting creates the sense of hierarchy. Because we cannot do whatever we want and create anything, we feel like creations and not gods. A soul is a piece of G-d that was formed as a creation, and we experience that because He chose to limit Himself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3
