blocks.text: The *igulim* express the simple desire, the first desire for a *dira b'tachtonim*, the first circle of the general will that colors everything that happens in the *seder hishtalshelus*. Then comes *chachma*, which decides how G-dliness will be transparent in the world and which things will not be. Then *bina* and the separation of things, and the *middos*: *chesed* creates something from nothing, and *gevura* makes things feel separate, as *Tanya* describes.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class starts line 7 at 15:06 ("and then it contracts...") and explains it from here; the line mark in the dump (26:01) is approximate.

blocks.text: The *igulim* have no specific form yet. G-d has an essential desire and taste, and wants something to express it externally: the *igulim* are the search for a vessel that fits that inner *ratzon*. Later, in *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*, the associations are formed. Like a person looking for a house, he knows he is looking but not yet what it is.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class starts line 7 at 15:06 ("and then it contracts...") and explains it from here; the line mark in the dump (26:01) is approximate.

blocks.text: We also look for ourselves. We sense an inner desire to be happy and to be our true selves, but we do not yet know how to express who we are in the outside world. In the same way the lights after the *tzimtzum* seek vessels. They surround as circles, encompassing, with nowhere to rest yet. The verse says the spirit of G-d was hovering over the water, an unrest seeking a form, which later formed the vessels in the days of creation.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: The class starts line 7 at 15:06 ("and then it contracts...") and explains it from here; the line mark in the dump (26:01) is approximate.

phrases.he: עד בחינת רצון ותענוג שבאבא ואמא שמתצמצמים ברצון ושכל והשגה, ג׳ ראשין דחכמה ובינה כו'
phrases.en: then it's expressed in the desire of *Abba* and *Ima*, the *chachma* and *bina* of *Atzilus*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: עד בחינת מדות ז׳ תחתונים דבינה
phrases.en: until that goes down to become the intellect for the emotions in the seven lower *sefiros* of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: From the *igulim* the process goes to the *yosher*. In *Adam Kadmon* the abstract inner desires are associated with something specific: the desire to feel at home becomes a desire for a house.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: A worldview channels the desire
blocks.text: A person has a picture of himself, of the world, and of his place in it. That worldview channels the inner desire into outer desires. So a person who wants to feel at home now wants a house.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Every person has the same essential desires: to be happy, to express creativity and contribute, to belong. How these are expressed depends on circumstances, and on each soul's nature and unique mission, which is shown to it in *Adam Kadmon*. Part of *chinuch* is to help a child express these in a healthy way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: A parent educates a child to want to learn, work and be kind. Once he has those good experiences he realizes it is what he wants. That takes effort, like striking flint for a spark.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The way G-d made the world, the easiest, laziest path may seem to get what one wants, but it does not fit who one is. Finding the right vessels takes work, just as exercise develops the body and study develops the mind.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: In *Adam Kadmon* G-d creates these associations. The Torah's wisdom and laws are the inner desires associated with specific details. Each soul starts the same but is shown its mission and its sparks, which gives it its personality and talents. The same goes for the angels, each formed by its mission, and then for the physical world.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: These essential desires become the specific desires revealed in the crown of *Atzilus*, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*. They are the pleasure and desire for G-dliness, the essential G-dly spark that is a person's true identity, and the desire is aligned with it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Abba* and *Ima*, the *chachma* and *bina* of *Atzilus*, pass it down to become the intellect of the seven lower *sefiros* of *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: עד בחינת קטנות מוחין דנה''י דאבא ואמא בזעיר אנפין כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: all the way down to the immature *mochin* of *netzach*, *hod*, *yesod* of *Abba* and *Ima* in *Zeir Anpin*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Atik Yomin* is the view that there is nothing except G-d. Its metaphor is *taanug*, delight, because delight is self-expression, so everything in the world is seen as G-d's self-expression. *Arich Anpin* sees the world as separate from G-d, yet still His will.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Chachma* sees the world as separate but transparent to G-d, totally *batel* to Him, like language that expresses only the will of the speaker. We see the wisdom in how He formed it. *Bina* sees the diversity, that each thing has a unique character and a particular expression that is not found in the all-encompassing oneness.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *middos*, as *Tanya* describes them. *Chesed* is creating something from nothing. *Gevura* makes it seem independent, as if it were separate from G-d. *Tiferes* is that G-d still reveals Himself through miracles and *tzaddikim*. *Netzach* is that once the world seems separate, we still feel independent, as in the sun, on which we depend totally.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Hod* is like *gevura*: instincts built into the body let us run on our own, like the animals of the fifth day, born knowing how to care for themselves. *Yesod* is *hashgacha prati*, and the people and mammals of the sixth day, who must be raised.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: All these *middos* express G-dliness higher than nature, and within them are *gadlus* and *ktanus*. Miracles within nature, as in the Purim story, are more *ktanus*. Miracles above nature are more *gadlus*, where one realizes that G-d truly runs the world. Viewing the world as having a fixed nature belongs to *Malchus*, which we will come to.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The immature view of *hashgacha prati* is that the world is separate and G-d can interfere in it with a miracle. The deeper view: everything is G-d's will, even the way every leaf blows, and a thing's very existence comes from His will, not just something He can influence. These are the more and less mature perspectives of *Zeir Anpin*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: People want things that are not what will make them happy. We see famous people who seem happy and think, if I had their money and fame, or were like them. This is very true of a child, who is impressionable, and even adults are.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Fiction
blocks.text: That is why it is important to be in a holy and proper environment. Fiction is fake, and even well-intentioned fiction subtly teaches things that are not true and makes wrong connections. A person whose life comes from complete fictions, with heroes who dodge bullets and always come out fine, is harmed by them. The whole idea of *chinuch* is *emes*: knowing who the person really is, and being honest about him and about the limits of the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: A farbrengen from the sixties
blocks.text: A *farbrengen* of the *Rebbe* from the sixties already says that the belief that kids should not be told what to do, only exposed to things and let choose, does damage; after twenty or thirty years one sees it. Kids want to be shown what to do, because a responsible adult sees who the child is better than the child does.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *Rambam*'s example is a child who does not want to learn to read, but who in truth does want to learn and express himself. The beginning is hard, and then it frees his mind to open books. Manners, sharing, self-discipline and restraint are the same: hard at first, and they help a person find and uncover who he really is.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: That is the job of a mature parent or educator, and *Torah* is similar: it sees the G-dly essence and spark that you really are, and does not impose what is not you.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Shevirat hakelim* is the disconnect in which what we think we are, and what we think will make us happy, is not right. That leads us to chase things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The truth should be said: the person is not who he thinks, and this will not make him happy. Today's society wants to keep people in their fiction and not break them out of it, because that is uncomfortable. It is not a kindness.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping generalisation about present-day society: a jab at its culture, softened. The point (say the truth; comfort is not kindness) stays.
sensitivity.publishable: The truth should be said: the person is not who he thinks, and this will not make him happy. Some people want to keep others in their fiction and not break them out of it, because that is uncomfortable. It is not a kindness.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: A person shifts out of a mistaken view of himself through two things: changing what he does, and changing how he thinks. Learning alone is not enough.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: A child afraid of the pool
blocks.text: A child afraid to get into the pool will not be convinced by talk. You have to get him to put his feet in the water, then more, and then to blow bubbles. Together with explanation of how it works, he gains confidence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: This is why *maaseh* is the main thing, and we say *naaseh* before *nishma*. As the *Sefer HaChinuch* says, the hearts are drawn after the actions: the way we act shapes how we feel and think. The foundation is acting the right way, through the mitzvos, and then the learning and understanding let us tune in and have the biggest effect. We need both.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *kabbalah* says action refines the outside of the *kli*, and learning refines the inside. We need both.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ומשם מתצמצם עוד בג' מדריגות דחב''ד חג''ת דזעיר אנפין כו',
phrases.en: And from there, from the *ktanus* of *mochin* that's going to be the intellect for *Zeir Anpin*, goes to the actual levels of *Chabad* *Chagat* of *Zeir Anpin* itself

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: עד בחינת חיצוניות הכלים דנצח והוד שבבחינת הבל החזה כו'
phrases.en: until, like the metaphor in a person, is that a person's feelings get expressed in their emotional state, in their heart, in their lungs

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שם מסתיים אור הרצון הפשוט שהיה כלול בהעלם עצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי כו'

blocks.text: From there the lower *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin* go on to its levels of *Chabad* and *Chagat*, down to the external vessels of *netzach* and *hod* in the breath of the chest, which you can hear in a person's voice.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The heart and the voice
blocks.text: In a person, the inner self plugs into the body: happiness or anxiety is felt in the heart and breath, and heard in the voice. So G-d's simple will is plugged in through *Adam Kadmon*, which creates the system of our reality.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: From there the will goes into *Atzilus*, where it creates the lights and vessels, and G-d chooses which things are only in His purview, such as creating something from nothing. He hides this, to make us feel independent, and the *middos* can each be reviewed from more and less mature perspectives. All of it is an expression of G-d's simple desire.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Why is it this way? Logic has no answer, because logic is based on a system, as if G-d were forced to act that way. Nothing forces Him. He chooses it. Even the ten *sefiros* are created because He wants them that way, so everything is an expression of His essential *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *Kuntres*, *Inyana shel Torat HaChassidus*, shows how seeing from the perspective of the essence shifts everything. Torah and *mitzvos* are not there to solve problems in the world; G-d created the world with its problems as an arena for our *avoda*. Likewise, a person does not value his gifts for their own sake, but as a piece of G-d: his life, health and wealth are opportunities, vessels to express G-dliness.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The logic of Torah is beyond logic; it is just G-d's will. Logic and reason are themselves created by G-d, and part of what He wants is for Torah and creation to have laws, reason and a system that we work within.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: That is part of the challenge G-d desired: to reveal G-dliness where there is a challenge, and to do it on our own, so we can understand the goal, strategize and develop, as in technology. Viewing things from the essence makes them all G-dly. This is the idea of this *hisbonenus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Yichud: the whole descent is one, and still Ein Sof
sections.summary: The whole descent happens in one step, because G-d and His *garmohi* (organs) are one. Even the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* are still *Ein Sof*, and the smallness of the *middos* at the end comes from the beginning.

phrases.he: והרי מכל רבוי פרטי ההשתלשלות הזאת, נעשה ונמשך בבת אחת
phrases.en: you could see how all this stuff, this whole process, becomes like in one step.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: מרצון שעלה בהעלם העצמות עד שבא במורגש בהבל הלב,
phrases.en: all the way to how the person feels in their heart

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: משום דאיהו וחיוהי וגרמוהי חד

blocks.text: Once a person understands these things, the whole process becomes one step, though it may take time. The *Kuntres Inyana shel Torat HaChassidus* does this: the *Rebbe* puts it all together.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: One desire in a person
blocks.text: A person's inner desire becomes one thing, reaching how he feels in his heart. With practice, anything in Torah, the world or ourselves is seen as G-d's will.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The phrase says that *Ayhu* and his *garmohi* are one. *Garmohi* means the organs, the *kelim*, and the *kelim* are one with G-d.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: פירוש איהו, בחינת עצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: it means His very essence of the *Ein Sof*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וחיוהי, בחינת עשר ספירות דהעלם וגלוי, כשלהבת כו'
phrases.en: and His lights, His life forces

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: עד עשר ספירות דזעיר אנפין כו'
phrases.en: all the way down to the ten the *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*, which is still the idea of a self-expression of a light

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וגרמוהי, בחינת הכלים דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: and the organs

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: חד, הכל בבחינת אין סוף עדיין
phrases.en: and it's all still really *Ein Sof*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Ayhu* is the very essence of the *Ein Sof*. *Chayohi*, His life forces, are the ten *sefiros* of concealment and revelation, like a flame from a coal: a self-expression of the hidden essence.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Down to the ten *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin* it is still a self-expression of light. The *garmohi*, the organs, are its vessels, its limited form. It is all one.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Free choice still inside
blocks.text: A person's choice is still his own expression. In the *nimshal*, it comes from G-d's will; it is all still *Ein Sof*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כי גם שבחינת הכלים, המגבילים למדות חיצוניות דלב זעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: even though the *kelim* that limit the *middos* in the external heart of *Zeir Anpin*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: הן בתכלית הקטנות לגבי ערך רוממות עצמות המדות שבבחינת מלכות דאין סוף,
phrases.en: even though those are completely immature

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: מכל מקום נחשב בחינת סוף לראש,
phrases.en: but that's still the end of the beginning

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש כו'
phrases.en: that G-d calls the generations from the head, from the beginning

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וסיומן בסוף הוא בבחינת קטנות המדות דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: and the end, in the the *siyum*, the completion, the end of that whole process is the these immature *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *kelim* that limit the *middos* of the external heart of *Zeir Anpin* are very small compared with the *middos* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. Still, they are the end that stands for the beginning. G-d is seen in miracles like those of Purim, and in the small everyday miracles people tell of, and one appreciates G-d that way even on that level.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Chabad* once did not tell miracle stories, because it seemed too immature. The *Rebbe* encouraged them. Even if a person is on that level and that is what he appreciates, his *emunah* is plugged in.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: That is why we tell the Chanukah story simply, to children. It turns on *emunah* and connects us to the belief that G-d is beyond the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The ten plagues, the splitting of the sea and the exodus express G-dliness, though we then believed in nature and had an immature view. They are vessels for G-dliness; bigger, more mature vessels, of seeing G-d in everything, take more work.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: As the verse says, G-d calls the generations from the head, from the beginning. The whole history and the whole *seder hishtalshelus*, from beginning to end, comes from the beginning, from the *Ein Sof*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The end of the whole process is the immature *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*, where G-dliness is revealed in small hints and sparks that we experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

sections.title: Small face and large face: the same makeup at different sizes
sections.summary: *Zeir Anpin* is the small face: it has the same intellect and *middos* as the large face, *Arich Anpin*, but they are expressed in small things. The same G-dliness is found in the smallest matter and in the greatest, and the chapter ends with *Adam Kadmon*, the highest of the three Adams.

phrases.he: ולכך נקרא זעיר אנפין קטנות הפנים,
phrases.en: and therefore *Zeir Anpin* is called a small face

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* is called the small face, *ktanus hapanim*, which is what the name means.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כאנפי זוטרי דתינוק קטן
phrases.en: like the small face of a small child

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: לגבי בחינת אנפי רברבי, זקן שקנה חכמה כו'
phrases.en: compared to a mature adult

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שזה תכלית הקטנות במוחין, וזה תכלית הגדלות
phrases.en: that the baby has the smallest, most immature *mochin*, intellect and understanding, and the wise adult has the ultimate maturity

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: מכל מקום משתווים בערך אדם,
phrases.en: but they're both a person

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: רק שזה נקרא אדם קטן וזה נקרא אדם הגדול כו',
phrases.en: just one is a small person, a young, immature person, and one is a large, adult, mature person

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: אבל ציור אופניו אחד הוא
phrases.en: but they have the same, the same makeup, the same, just like physically they're the same face, and emotionally, at least they're the same

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כי בקטן מדותיו גם כן על פי שכל ורצון הנעלם כו',
phrases.en: because in the child, their intellect is also they're also guided by their understanding and what they want

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: רק שבא בתכלית הקטנות מאד
phrases.en: but it's just expressed in the child in a very immature way

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: ובאדם הגדול מדותיו גדולים על פי רוחב שכלו ורצונו הרמה והנשגבה ביותר כו'
phrases.en: based on the breadth of his knowledge and understanding

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The small face of a child
blocks.text: A child has the full makeup of a person, with wisdom, intellect and emotions, but it is all for small things. As a person grows he has the same makeup, but it is triggered by bigger things. So G-dliness and *emunah* can be found in the smallest thing as well as the greatest.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: From the walls down to the knobs
blocks.text: A person's taste plugs into big things, the walls, house and roof, and equally into the drapes and little knobs. G-dliness is found in everything.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true of our *avoda*: from the biggest *mitzvah* to the smallest, from the deepest ideas of *Kabbalah* to the simple stories of the *Torah*, all have equal G-dliness, and *emunah* connects to them. A little child who eats a *latke* with oil, with *emunah*, connects to the beginning, though in a very small way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *Kuntres HaHispaalus* describes the *yechida* coming out on the levels of *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*, *chaya* and *yechida*. The simplest is feeling that it is *Shabbos* and one keeps it: the *yechida* feeling the holiness, even without deeper love and fear.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The same essence is expressed in the greatest *tzaddik*, like *Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai*, whose whole life was G-dliness, only in a larger, more mature way. Once one sees what the essence looks like, one finds it in everything.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The baby has the smallest, most immature *mochin*, and the wise adult has ultimate maturity. Both are a person, the same in makeup, the same face, and emotionally the same. Only one is small and immature, the other large and mature.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: In the child, the *middos* are also guided by his understanding and by what he wants. If he thinks he is going to lose his lollipop, he gets upset, just as an adult gets upset about losing a fortune, or a *tzaddik* gets upset about something spiritual. It is expressed in a very immature way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The adult's *middos* are great, based on the breadth of his understanding and elevated desire. As people grow they go from candy to money and honor, and finally to wanting the truth because it is true and doing right because it is right, as the *Rambam* describes.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: כך ערך קטנות המדות דזעיר אנפין, שהם המדות שמצומצמין בקטנות השכל דנצח והוד כו',
לגבי בחינת אריך אנפין שנקרא אנפי רברבי
phrases.en: versus the *Arich Anpin*, which means the large face

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: גדלות הפנים והמוחין דזקן שקנה חכמה
ממקור החכמה הנעלמה, שלמעלה מקרומא כו'
phrases.en: this source of *chochma* that comes from higher than the *karoma*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת שכל הנעלם שברצון הנעלם כו',
phrases.en: which is that hidden subconscious desire

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא שרש הנאצלים כו'
phrases.en: that's the source of the *nitzolim*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וכן גם המדות שברצון ושכל הנעלם דאריך אנפין, הוא בבחינת קטנות הערך לגבי בחינת אדם הגדול יותר, והוא בחינת אדם קדמון שנקרא אדם דבריאה כו'
phrases.en: the perspective of *Arich Anpin*, of the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, is also called immature compared to the deeper, higher perspective of *Adam Kadmon*, which is called the *Adam diBeriya*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: (וכידוע דזעיר אנפין נקרא אדם דעשיה ואריך אנפין נקרא אדם דיצירה ואדם קדמון אדם דבריאה
ובכל אחד יש עשר ספירות בהעלם וגלוי כו'
phrases.en: and each of them have ten *sefiros*, again, in *helem* and *gilui*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב לכבודי, שהוא מלכות דאין סוף, בראתיו – אדם קדמון, יצרתיו – עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין, אף עשיתיו – בחינת זעיר אנפין שנאמר בו, נעשה אדם בצלמינו כו')
phrases.en: that for My glory I've created them, formed them, and made them, that the glory is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The prize and the hook
blocks.text: This is the *mashal* for *gadlus* and *ktanus*. A small child expresses his desire for extrinsic things; as a person matures he appreciates intrinsic value. A child can do the right thing for a prize, and the prize is only a hook. Underneath, he is plugging in his essence and *emunah*, just as the adult does, but he needs *kelim*: tests and checklists that make it tangible.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: In a person, the immature intellect of the *middos* gets through the day, based on what is in front of him. *Arich Anpin*, the large face, is the mature view of what really matters, beyond the day-to-day.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The source is *chochma* higher than the *karoma*. The reason logic makes sense, and the reason I want these things and care about them, is who I am, which is higher than logic: G-d created me that way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The subconscious *sechel* comes from the hidden desire, the *ratzon hamuchlat* like a person's taste. It is the source of the *nitzolim*, and of how G-dliness is expressed in Torah, *mitzvos*, souls and angels.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: All of these are very limited and small. Why does it matter whether I slaughter in one way or another, or whether tefillin are exactly so? Every detail of the world is an expression of this higher, transcendent *ratzon*. We can learn to see it, and that is developing maturity; or we can fail to see it, which is *ktanus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *middos* within the hidden will and understanding of *Arich Anpin* are also immature, compared with the greater man, *Adam Kadmon*, which is called *Adam diBeriya*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* is *Adam diAsiya*, *Arich Anpin* is *Adam diYetzira*, and *Atik* and *Adam Kadmon* are *Adam diBeriya*. The *nimshal* is in the *Kuntres Inyana shel Torat HaChassidus*, which explains *peshat*, *remez*, *drush* and *sod* according to *Chassidus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The *peshat* of *Chassidus* is like *Adam diAsiya* in the general sense: the purpose of my life is to bring *Elokus* into the world, and I value my life because of that. *Yetzira* is the relation of soul and body across the whole world, renewed every day, like *Arich* and *Atik* of *Atzilus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The essence of the *Torah* is that G-d creates the whole world, soul and body, as an arena for *Torah* and *mitzvos*. *Torah* expresses His will, higher than *sechel*: that is the perspective of *Adam Kadmon*, the *Adam diBeriya*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Each of the ten *sefiros* has its hidden and revealed sides: the inner self-expression, and the way it is expressed externally in the vessels.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The verse says "for My glory I created them": *Adam Kadmon*, formed *Atik* and *Arich*, made *Zeir Anpin*, and made man in Our image. The glory is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.1 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: As we come down from *Adam Kadmon* to *Arich Anpin*, *Abba* and *Ima*, and *Zeir Anpin*, the will goes from very big and mature in *Arich* to very small and immature in *Zeir Anpin*. *Arich* compared with *Adam Kadmon* is immature and considered small.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32 and explains the descent of lines 26 to 31 again, from Adam Kadmon down; the Rambam mashal recurs.

blocks.text: The *Rambam*'s *mashal*: a child does not see the intrinsic value of learning, so he gets prizes and candy. A mature person learns to know the truth, and to do what is right, because it is right.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The prize and the hook
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32 and explains the descent of lines 26 to 31 again, from Adam Kadmon down; the Rambam mashal recurs.

blocks.text: In *Zeir Anpin* you get what you deserve, based on what you do. In *Arich Anpin* is the intrinsic mercy of the thirteen attributes: we can always return.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32 and explains the descent of lines 26 to 31 again, from Adam Kadmon down; the Rambam mashal recurs.

blocks.text: Going back to *Adam Kadmon* is higher still: the whole reason G-d created *Torah*, *mitzvos*, the world and its challenges, and both inclinations, is for *Yisroel* and for us. The higher the level, the more mature the perspective.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 033.2 opens before line 32 and explains the descent of lines 26 to 31 again, from Adam Kadmon down; the Rambam mashal recurs.

sections.title: The map: a small drawing of a large thing still holds all of it
sections.summary: A map draws the earth in small lines, and the small drawing still holds everything, shrunk down. The world is built the same way, with the same pattern at every scale.

phrases.he: והוא על דרך משל ציור קוין שעושין בקטנות לדבר גדול,
phrases.en: the analogy for this is like when you make lines to represent a large thing

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו דמיון המפה לכדור הארץ כו'
phrases.en: like when you make a map for the earth

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שעם כל זה יש בציור זה הכל
phrases.en: Even though it's very small, it has within it everything that's in the real world

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לא נעדר אפילו כקוצו של יו''ד כו',
phrases.en: It's all there

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: רק שהוא בקטנות מאד,
phrases.en: it's just that it's very small

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ומה שמצוייר בו קו קטן בכדור הארץ הוא אורך נהר ת''ק פרסא
phrases.en: What is a small line on your map, on the actual world, could be a river that's 500 miles long

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא כו'

blocks.text: The analogy is a drawing of small lines that stands for something large, like a map of the earth. The earth is far bigger than the paper, and even a globe on your desk is a small picture of the world. The models and systems we build to understand reality and to decide what to do are a little caricature of it; they never fully capture it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: There is also the idea of macrocosm and microcosm. G-d makes each person a little world, so a life is like all of creation, and each year and each day of it is a microcosm too. It is the same with the drawing: nothing is missing, not even a little; it is all there, shrunk down.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The coastline of Norway
blocks.text: Fractals are a good example. Certain equations generate shapes that, when you zoom in on their edges, show the same kind of pattern repeating at every scale, never exactly the same and without end. A coastline is like this. Ask how long the coast of Norway is and there is no easy answer: measured with a kilometer stick you get one length, with a meter stick a much longer one, and with a millimeter stick longer still, because the coast folds in on itself over and over. So G-d created the world with this infinite complexity, and you can zoom in and out and find the same structure at different scales.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is only very small. A short line on the map can stand for a river five hundred miles long on the real earth, and so on.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The Greeks showed that the earth is round long before the Middle Ages. Some people in the Middle Ages believed it was flat, but he doesn't think that was ever really a universal belief.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The child: the same makeup as the adult, at a smaller and less mature scale
sections.summary: A young child has the same *middos* as a mature elder, expressed immaturely. The same pattern is reproduced at each step of the descent, as a child and as a sprout show.

phrases.he: וכך על דרך משל המדות דקטנות דתינוק
phrases.en: And so in a similar way, metaphorically, the emotions of a young child

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לגבי מדות דזקן בן ע' כו'
phrases.en: have the same makeup as a mature elder that's 70 years old

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The basic makeup of the *middos* is the same in a young child and in a mature elder: there is *chesed* and *gevura*, love and fear. What a child loves and fears is very immature. A mature, wise adult also loves and fears, but on a different level.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The prize and the hook
blocks.text: The Rambam's *mashal*: a child learns for candy and out of fear of punishment. A mature adult sees his potential and value, and fears it will be wasted; he wants him to grow into who he really is. He builds the whole system, but cares about the child's potential, not the candy.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Reality has layers. Our world is set up like a tutorial, where G-d educates us and we educate ourselves. Some small things that happen to us matter only in the moment, while other things matter more.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The ice cream on the floor
blocks.text: If an ice cream falls on the floor, you are upset in the moment, but in twenty years you will not care. Bigger things, like the mortgage, are real too. But at the end of life, a person does not regret not earning more; he asks whether he connected to the people he loves and did meaningful things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A deeper perspective: the soul asks whether it did its mission, connected to G-d, and did what it is meant to do.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d sets up reality as a fractal pattern. Each cell is its own little creature, and the cells form an organism; a human being is not complete alone. We form families, families form society, and society is part of the human race over a long time. Zoom out and bigger things appear; at bigger time scales what matters, and how the *middos* measure it, is very different. That holds in time, in space and spiritually.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Air, water and food
blocks.text: An immature view says everything depends on what we do and deserve; a deeper view says G-d loves us, as you see in what we need. Food takes work, water is easier to get, and air is everywhere. We can go without air far less time than without water, and without food longer than without water. The less essential a thing is, the more it depends on what we do.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Allowance and chores
blocks.text: G-d gives us existence, a soul, value, talents and personality for free. Within our needs, physical and spiritual, some things do depend on what we do. It is like telling a child: I'll give you an allowance if you do your chores, but I won't withhold your basic needs if you don't. That would be abusive.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d creates reality with mature perspectives deep down and immature ones at the surface, where things depend on what we do and we have free choice, within a smaller realm. We need not be embarrassed to get things free, the bread of shame: G-d gives us the ability to earn it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: A child who helps
blocks.text: A parent often does not need a child's help, but asking is a kindness: the child feels important and learns. So G-d giving us Torah, mitzvos and a mission, on our immature level, is itself a kindness.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d does not need our mitzvos. He created the whole world, and He could have made it perfect.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He made the world imperfect so that we would have something to perfect, and made us unsatisfied, so that we would not just sit in Eden munching leaves and berries. The drive to do more, to invent, and to build agriculture and societies is a double-edged sword. It brings good and bad, the tree of knowledge of good and bad: it lets us accomplish a great deal, and it brings strife, jealousy and war.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו כח המוליד
phrases.en: another example of this is the power of reproduction

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: בדומה לו כו'
(וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין בוצין בוצין כו')
phrases.en: like it explains elsewhere to the *Gemara*, where it talks about these little kids who were saying things that were very wise

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The child as a smaller copy
blocks.text: Another example is the power of reproduction: a child is a little, immature version of ourselves, like us but small, and still growing. The descent from *Adam Kadmon* to *Arich Anpin* to *Zeir Anpin* is the same pattern, reproduced on a smaller and less mature scale.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The gourd sprout
blocks.text: He says the *Gemara* elsewhere speaks of little children who said very wise things, and that you can tell from a sprout what the plant will become: whether it grows fast and strong, or has a kink that will deform it. He thinks it is a pumpkin, or some sort of gourd. In the same way, little children already have a personality, each one unique, but it is all still small, undefined and immature.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The nimshal: the same middos, contracted, and all of it still transparent to G-d
sections.summary: The *middos* of *Atzilus* are the same as those above them, only contracted. The Name shows that the whole descent stays transparent to G-d's will, even at the smallest level.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בחינת המדות דאדם דאצילות, דגם שבאים בצמצום היותר אחרון לגבי בחינת המדות דאדם קדמון ואריך אנפין כו',
אבל מכל מקום הכל אחד,
phrases.en: so it's all really one thing

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: רק שבא מן בחינת האריכות היותר מופלג אל הקיצור היותר מופלג
phrases.en: it just went from the biggest length to being very small

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The *middos* of *Atzilus* come from a very late contraction of those of *Adam Kadmon* and *Arich Anpin*, but it is all one thing: it went from the biggest length to being very small.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Going up the chain it is far more infinite. Coming down, G-d limited it to ten *sefiros* with vessels and a system of measure for measure: good and bad, G-dly and not. That is Torah and mitzvos as we know them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It says that Torah is a kind of outflow of the wisdom above, a very small, immature thing. Our world is one very small possibility out of infinite possibilities; G-d could have created infinite universes. Still, within our world there are infinite possibilities.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Within our world there is free choice, and G-d's infinite creative expression reveals infinity within what He creates here.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Speaking in a language
blocks.text: It is like a language: once you are given a certain language, you can say whatever you want in it. There is freedom of expression, but it is bounded and limited.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So as it comes down, it keeps its essential character of being G-dly and infinite. It is just expressed in a very small way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Down to the physical world, everything is alive, a direct revelation of G-dliness: the life that creates and sustains it, with its infinite quality. Even a single cell is mind-bogglingly complex, like a whole city of life and activity.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.question: Why talk about infinite worlds if we cannot wrap our minds around one world, or even one cell?
blocks.text: There are two sides to *hisbonenus*. One is what we can understand, the level of *bina*: the creation in front of us, which we have to understand. The other is a sense of wonder and humility before the G-dly source that creates us, called "nothing" because it transcends everything we know.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We cannot fathom what is beyond time, space and worlds like ours. We need the humility to recognize that we do not know everything, and tend to focus only on what we do know. Most of what there is to know we do not know, even about our own world. So when we understand our world, we should not feel we have got everything.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This whole world is just a little nothing example to G-d. He is revealed in it, but only if you do not limit Him to it. If you think it is all there is, you make G-d into the universe, and limit Him.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The twelve-dollar bouquet
blocks.text: Flowers given to show love are insulting if they are taken to put your value at a twelve-dollar bouquet. But if you say, 'I recognize that I cannot express this, so I express it in this token way,' the gift is meaningful.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This ties to the idea, which he says appears elsewhere, that we must feel inadequate: however perfect our *avodah* becomes, it never does Him justice. Letting go of thinking we can fully achieve it is what lets us reach the perfection we can reach, since then we do what we can. Thinking we can do Him justice is an insult.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: If I think G-d is *Adam Kadmon*, or some high thing I can understand, that is *avoda zara* (idolatry). If I recognize that I cannot understand Him, and do my best with these tools to connect to Him, I keep my faith plugged into the intellect, and that makes it G-dly. That is one reason to recognize these things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: (וזה שכתוב מה שמו מה שם בנו
phrases.en: and this is what it says, 'What is His name and what is His son's name?'

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: – מה שמו, מ''ה דאדם קדמון – מה שם בנו, בחינת זעיר אנפין כו'
וכמו שכתוב בכמה דוכתי)
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere in other places

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The verse asks, "What is His name, and what is His son's name?" The first is the Name *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*. The son's name is *Zeir Anpin*, the level we are talking about now.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That Name is how things are *bittul* and transparent to G-d's will. It goes down from Adam Kadmon to Arich Anpin and then to Zeir Anpin, as is explained elsewhere, in Kabbalah and Chassidus.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: At the highest level G-d is infinite and can do whatever He wants. Coming down the chain it seems that rules limit Him, but that transparency and that freedom is still revealed.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In our world He does miracles; they do not completely destroy the laws of nature, but work within our world. He created it, and He can make things happen the way He wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The summary: one desire, from its essence down to the physical world
sections.summary: The whole descent is one act of G-d's desire, from its essence down to the physical world. Learning it should supercharge the simple words we say in davening, and the same pattern repeats in the microcosm, down to us.

phrases.he: והיינו כללות ההתבוננות בכל אשר חפץ יהו״ה בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: And this is the general *hisbonenus* that when we say that everything G-d desires, He does, we should recognize

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: עשה בשמים שהוא בחינת זעיר אנפין
אש ומים – חסד וגבורה דקטנות דאצילות כו'
(עד בחינת שמים דעשיה)
phrases.en: and then coming all the way down to the world of

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is the general *hisbonenus*: that everything G-d desires, He does, goes all the way back to *Atzmus Ein Sof*. He chose to create the world; nothing compelled Him to.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He chose to reveal Himself through the *sefiros*, and to combine lights and vessels, so that He would have a dwelling in the lower worlds, to be accomplished through man.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The ten *sefiros* are the idea of man, built with ten powers. G-d decided that we would have intrinsic value, and also that we would have to work, and that there is repentance if we go wrong. So we hold two things: an essential connection that never changes, and a conditional one that lets us work and grow.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He set it the same way in the microcosm, down to us. We should treat our children and the people we love this way: love them for their intrinsic value, and challenge them to grow because we love them. We have to balance the two.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d created the whole system, down to *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*: how Torah and mitzvos work, what is good and bad, what is G-dly. It is also how our world works; some things are good to eat and some are poison.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In our world *chesed* and *gevura* were created from nothing, and we are given a sense of independence from *gevura*. G-d set this balance up very specifically: from one side we feel His presence, from the other we feel independent. That is *Zeir Anpin*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* is fire and water, *gevura* and *chesed*: G-d gives us everything for free, and demands something of us, the *gevura* side. The two are balanced very specifically, in a smaller, more immature way within *Atzilus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Fire is *gevura* and water is *chesed*, he agrees. He thinks the verse gives that order because G-d first wanted to create the world with *gevura*, saw that it would not endure, and mixed in mercy.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Perhaps this is connected: the main purpose of creation is our *avoda*; otherwise we would not need a world. To do it successfully we need a foundation of security, knowing that we matter and that G-d loves us. That is the *chesed*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The game
blocks.text: Another analogy: you make a game for someone to play. You set up the whole game and give them everything, but its purpose is to challenge them. Maybe that is the reason.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: When G-d created the physical world, the heavens, the sun gives energy and warmth, and the rain comes down, all of it given to us. But we have to do things: plow and plant to grow more crops. Even what grows on its own, like nuts and berries, takes effort to find. So life and energy are given to us almost without limit, and locally we have to work to get them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Water in the world
blocks.text: People talk about a fresh-water crisis, but you cannot really run out: water evaporates and rains back down. There can be a local shortage, with no clean water where you need it, but you cannot really waste water, because it goes somewhere: through rock, or back up by evaporation.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Our existence comes directly from G-d, without intermediaries: that is unlimited G-dly energy, the *chesed*. Then there are things like the sun, which is *netzach*, and comes through a *kli*, a vessel.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Other things depend on us. Rain sometimes comes and sometimes does not, so we must adapt and save up for a drought or a harsh winter, because there are seasons. This is the balance of the two.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Again it is like a game or a tutorial, for us to learn and grow, as individuals, as a society and as humanity, toward peace and prosperity. On a deeper level it is to discover truth for its own sake, to explore the world, and to appreciate its beauty and G-d's wisdom.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לפי שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן,
phrases.en: because the beginning is wedged in the end

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מחכמה בראש דאדם קדמון עד חכמה בסוף מדות דזעיר אנפין

blocks.text: Because the beginning is wedged in the end, the descent runs from the *chachma* at the head of *Adam Kadmon* down to the *chachma* at the end of the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: How much our actions matter, and how much effort we need, physically and spiritually, is tuned in *Zeir Anpin* from the *chachma* of *Atzilus*, and originally from the *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*, because G-d wants a *dira b'tachtonim*, a dwelling in the lower worlds, where we do our *avoda*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In *davenen*, take the simple meaning of the words: G-d runs the world and everything in it. With this understanding of the whole descent behind it, you daven with the simple faith of a child, and that faith deepens.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Instead of only imagining it the way a child does, the understanding deepens the faith. G-d is beyond the rules of time and space, even beyond the *sefiros*, and He sets it all up. Nothing is an accident; He made the world exactly the way He wants it. So I should have faith, and trust that He knows what He is doing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: I am not an accident either: G-d chose to create me on purpose, flaws included. I am meant to be human, with potential and flaws, and to struggle, and that is what He wants. I am not meant to be perfect. Life is constant growth.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Realizing this lets me tune in to what I am doing more powerfully. As we talked about, a soul can come down for seventy or eighty years just to do a favor for another person.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d did not have to create the world; He chose it out of a desire for kindness, which is the same as wanting a dwelling in the lower worlds. This moment, with this chance to help a person, is the justification for the whole creation.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So in davening, this should give me a deeper faith and trust in G-d, and a deeper sense of my mission. I can accept my flaws, not as a fallback but as what G-d wants. I will fail at some things, succeed at others, and struggle on the front line in some places; I should not feel bad about that.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: I think this is one of the main reasons *Tanya* is called the book of the in-betweens. It is a mistake to see myself as a righteous or wicked person, at a complete end point. I am in the middle of my mission, and should value living in the moment and connecting to what I am doing now.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The Rebbe's gaze
blocks.text: People talk about going in to the Rebbe, and how piercing his eyes were. I think a big part of it was that he was totally focused; nothing else was there in that moment. He saw that G-d can do whatever He wants and had chosen this person and this encounter, so he asked how to help: what to say, what to encourage, what call to make, how to help the G-dly spark in front of him. That is the whole purpose of creation, right here.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is one example of *hisbonenus*. It can be plugged into many things, including the simple meaning of the words and a great deal of davening.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Thinking about the specific ideas of the earlier chapters while praying is a distraction. Once you have learned them and put them into the condensed form, that learning should supercharge your sense of the words of davening.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: *Hayom Yom* says that davening can be just one blessing, or one verse of Psalms, said with real sincerity, faith and feeling, but getting there takes a lot of learning first. During davening we are not meant to think through all the levels; that is done before davening.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: At the simple meaning of the words, all these levels should come together to make the ideas more powerful. This is what he is now showing: how to plug it into one line of *davenen*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: He takes a line from *davenen*, from *Tehillim*: whatever G-d desires He does, in the heavens, the earth, the seas and all the depths. This psalm is one of the Hallelujah psalms, and this is its theme: G-d chose the Jewish people, lifted us up, and took us out of Egypt.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: What does it mean that G-d chose us? First, recognize that G-d runs the world and can do whatever He wants. So I should not be affected by nature.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: I have a body bound by nature, but also a G-dly spark beyond time and space, where I can find the ability to be altruistic, to want truth because it is true, and to do right because it is right.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That part connects to *Ein Sof* and to the purpose of the *dira b'tachtonim*. Redemption is everything revealing its true essence: that is the primordial will. I should find that unity in myself and see it in everyone; that is G-d's real desire, that it be revealed.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Everything has a G-dly spark, and its being revealed is the real perfection and purpose of the thing. Seeing that, I see G-d's desire in things, to liberate them, and I do not look at the world only through my bodily needs.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Manis Friedman put it well: "You can go through life thinking about what I need, or being needy, or thinking about what I'm needed for." The animal soul is needy; the G-dly soul needs nothing, and asks how it can contribute.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: How can I reveal this G-dliness, the beauty that is inherent in everything and especially in every person? Seeing that this is G-d's desire is what drives everything. Then we come down to Adam Kadmon, where all the rules of reality are created: people, effort, logic, Torah and mitzvos. In Adam Kadmon I realize that G-d is choosing to set that up.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: I do a mitzvah not to solve a problem in the world: G-d set up the world with that problem so that I could solve it. The real purpose cannot come from the created world; it comes from something higher, and the world is its arena.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: One could see Torah as a manual: G-d created an imperfect world and gave us a guide for good living. No, it goes much deeper. Learning Torah and doing mitzvos connects us to the Creator, who is totally beyond the world. That gives integrity: we do not weigh whether it pays off, since this is why things were created.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The newcomer in town
blocks.text: The Rebbe gives an example: someone moves to a town where he competes for another person's business. One person can do *hisbonenus* and see that his income for the year was already set on Rosh Hashanah, so he is not threatened and has faith and trust. A deeper person sees an opportunity: he knows what it is like to start out, so he goes to help the newcomer and show him the ropes.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That is a G-dly perspective: not using G-d to protect me from someone who threatens me. Seeing my mission differently changes what my *middos* fear or are excited about in the same situation. When I am able to create, I say, "I can create a better situation; I can help somebody."

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is not a zero-sum game. From the world's view it looks closed: if he gains, I lose. From a G-dly view it is infinite, and if we cooperate it can be even better.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Physically it is better, but the main thing is not even that. We are here to contribute and to help people, not just to compete and survive.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This connects to *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*: it is never too late. If I mess up, I can always change. That is the thirteen attributes of mercy, a sense of forgiveness and acceptance of people, which comes from this perspective.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is still a little lower, because I judge people by what they do. Still, I believe people can always grow and return. The deeper view is that even if they do not change, they are valuable.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Fixed and growth mindsets
blocks.text: Some successful people are hard on themselves, and that can lead to success. But there is a fixed mindset and a growth mindset. "I am a success only if I am here" is unhealthy and counterproductive to growth. I think most really successful people have a growth mindset: growth is the point, and they compete with themselves, not an outside measure.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Growth is what life is about. Successful people push themselves to do more, not because they will finally arrive, but because they have a deeper need to challenge themselves and express unlimited potential. When a person starts competing with others, he becomes afraid to fail and afraid to try new things, and that shuts everything down.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: As we learned from *Keser* down to *Abba* and *Ima*: my intellect and belief systems are not real things. Intellect is almost a game; you can make anything make sense. Many perspectives are valid, as in the theory of relativity, and that is true in general too.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is not correct to think "I am better" or "this is better," since it depends on the perspective: whatever is different is good for something and worse for something else. The same goes for the systems we build to understand reality, in math, science or Torah. No system captures reality perfectly; they are useful tools.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A logic, system or grading system can help us challenge ourselves, but we should not believe in it too much. G-d creates the logic of the world and of Torah for a deeper purpose: to be helpful toward that goal.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We should use our beliefs and our logic intentionally, to create a helpful way of viewing things. Judging people by a system, saying 'it says here he is wrong, he is bad,' is unhealthy: it uses a system to cast people aside. Saying of myself, 'I'm a failure because I didn't do this or that,' is an unhealthy use of logic too.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That is the idea of having faith. If the Jewish people could believe only what made sense to them, they would never have left Egypt: how could they go into the desert with the Egyptians chasing them? How is that possible?

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: If we cannot accept that there are things beyond what we know, we keep getting the same results. We must connect to G-d's desire, which is higher than our understanding. He is more creative than we are; we do not have to understand how it is possible.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Learning to ride a bike
blocks.text: A small child who keeps falling off a bike cannot imagine riding it. But after ten hours of practice he will ride, and that makes a new reality for him.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Could I, ten years ago, have imagined where I am today, what I would know and how I would feel? We do not know our own potential, let alone the potential of all reality.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d can do what He wants; He is far more creative than we are, with many possibilities beyond what we know. We can use our intellect to grow, but should never limit G-d to it. Part of this is accepting who we are.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d chose me and gave me my talents and position, so I should not feel bad about who I am. He chose the Jewish people too and gave us a role. Everybody has a unique job; I should not think I am better than anybody, yet see the infinite value of my own role. That is *bina*, diversity, versus *chachma*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On one side, *chachma* asks for humility. Moshe did not consider himself better even than a gentile idolater, because that person may be serving what G-d made him for better than I serve my own mission; so how could I judge? On the other side, I must appreciate my uniqueness and be confident in it. That is the *bina* side.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Appreciating others' uniqueness starts with appreciating myself: my culture and heritage. As a Jew I should be proud that I am a Jew, and as a person I should celebrate my talents. On one hand I need humility; on the other, in a certain unique way I am better than everybody, since G-d gave me talents nobody else has.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So there is *chachma* and *bina*, depending on which world you look at. On a simple physical level we are all people, but we are all physically different.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On a spiritual level you can look at it all the way up to *Atzilus*, with the Jewish people and Torah; or spiritual versus physical, infinite versus finite. It is a mistake to think one is better: from the perspective of *Atzilus*, both are equally revelations of G-dliness, and each has a unique advantage, so I appreciate each separately.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Coming down to *Atzilus*: G-d runs the world and does what He wants, and He chose us and took us out of Egypt. We have a unique make-up, so that to do our mission we follow Torah and mitzvos. The Rebbe describes it as seeing a color nobody else can see.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We live as Jewish people in a unique reality, different from everybody else. G-d chose to give us a certain character, heritage and history. That colors who we are, gives us a unique mission, and gives us certain *middos* of what is good and bad for us.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So we do not eat non-kosher food, and keeping Shabbos is important for us. For somebody else it does not matter if they eat pork or work on Shabbos; it is good for them. In theory one soul is like another, but in practice we were created with this nature, history and heritage, and we decide based on it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In my own life: as a child I was told I can be whatever I want, and in a way that is true. But here I am, with my past, situation, abilities and challenges, and I have to figure out what is right now. It does not matter what I could have done in theory; that is what G-d wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: These are examples of this *hisbonenus*: understanding the levels helps me embrace that G-d runs the world, that He chose us, that we are His chosen people, and that I have a unique mission.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: I should embrace that I was born in a certain time, place and family, with a certain past, and that today I feel a certain way, with certain challenges. G-d wants me to find what is right and wrong within this.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Those are the *middos* as they apply to me in the microcosm, and that is all He wants from me, and it is great. I do not have to be Moshe; I can be Zusha, as long as I am true to who I am now.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: As long as I plug in, feel my G-dly spark, and see how it looks in this situation right now, that is perfect. That is all He wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Nineteen instead of twenty
blocks.text: Take a person who doesn't keep Shabbos. Every Shabbos he smokes a pack of cigarettes, and says, 'I'm going to smoke 19 instead of 20.' Perfect. That could be better than someone who keeps Shabbos perfectly.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

sensitivity.publishable: Take a person who doesn't keep Shabbos. Every Shabbos he is cutting back a little on one bad habit, and says, 'I'm going to do one less than last week.' Perfect. That could be better than someone who keeps Shabbos perfectly.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The example makes a real point (incremental progress is perfect for where a person is), but it uses smoking and calls it perfect. Decide whether the smoking stays in the public text or only the publishable version is printed.
sensitivity.publishableTitle: Cutting back one step at a time

blocks.text: If keeping Shabbos is easy for me, what am I doing to put in effort, to work and grow, and to help somebody else? Am I really plugging these values into my situation, whatever it is? It has both sides: accept the challenges, and not be satisfied with my successes, but push myself to grow. It goes both ways.

blocks.text: This verse, *min ha'olam ve'ad ha'olam* (from the world to the world), is "Blessed is G-d, the G-d of Israel." Here Israel is *Yisroel Saba*, the *middos* of *chachma*, the Zeir Anpin of *chachma*, going back to *Adam Kadmon*, of whom it says, "I created him."

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The microcosm of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* in the general worlds: *Adam Kadmon* is like *Beriya*, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* like *Yetzira*, and *Zeir Anpin* like *Asiya*. The macrocosm we are learning now, *yichuda ila'a*, is reflected in the microcosm.

blocks.text: We have been talking about *yichuda ila'a*: G-d decided what He wants and how He will reveal Himself, how He will make up the *sefiros* and *Atzilus*, and all of that replays itself in the microcosm, through *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d does whatever He wants in the physical heavens, the sun and sunspots and the weather, all the way down to the physical growth of plants, animals and people, and to climate change. G-d runs it all, based on how He chooses to run the world every moment.

blocks.text: The rest of the book deals with this half of the *seder hishtalshelus*. The point: learning all this should condense and supercharge the simple words we say.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In *Hayom Yom* there are three parts to hisbonenus: during learning, before davening, and during davening. During learning we focus on the intellect, the *bina* side, to understand.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Before davening we think about the life of the idea, which I believe is its *chachma*: how it shows up all over the place, and what lies beyond our understanding, with humility.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Then during davening we come with a *Keser* (crown), appreciating the G-dliness and our faith, as we come to speak to G-d, our Father.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/Ch 33/033.2 Shaar HaYichud ch 33 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So imagine plugging our faith into it, and saying the words with all this understanding, so that we really appreciate what we are saying, unlock that faith, and see how to apply it in our lives.
